product_from_film: Index by Parallel proposes a model where content owners can see the value of their content to AI agents and get paid.
explains_well: The change from browsing the open web to receiving answers from agents is expressed through a consistent network of dots.
unclear: The film does not show how a content owner joins, how content value is measured, or how payment happens.
scenario: A history of the open web becomes an argument for new economics, ending with Index and payment for content owners.
product_clear_basis: The creator value statement at 79s is followed by agents and payment wording around 82–83s.

scenes.action: A point, small text, connecting nodes and a historical web diagram describe the internet starting small and becoming more.
scenes.design: Dark field, fine white lines and tiny centered copy.
scenes.purpose: Establish the origin of the network.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 0–13s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: Many colored dots fill the frame; words refer to freedom, creativity, connections and research.
scenes.design: Dense color field with gaps and small text.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 13–23s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: White paper with feed holes contains an orange dot; a central orange hub gains radiating lines as a new user is introduced.
scenes.design: Paper texture, black nodes and orange emphasis.
scenes.purpose: Introduce a change in how the web is used.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 23–30s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: A dotted path becomes a node grid with a search-like pill. Dots gather below the tilted pill as old business model wording appears.
scenes.design: Minimal diagram states replace photographic examples.
scenes.purpose: Show an agent/search layer changing the network.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 30–41s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: Dots become gray and boxed; a circular white area shrinks against darkness as the opportunity is described as shrinking.
scenes.design: Constrained grids and a closing circular field.
scenes.purpose: Give the economic problem a spatial form.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 41–51s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: An orange dot and line lead to an orange field, white circle, connected network and radial grid.
scenes.design: Strong orange reset with expanding diagram states.
scenes.purpose: Turn the story toward a new possibility.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 51–62s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: Small text says the economics need a new model. A striped globe and Index wording appear, followed by repeated INDEX BY PARALLEL typography that condenses to a logo.
scenes.design: Paper background, geometric mark and repeated type.
scenes.purpose: Name the proposed model and brand.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 62–77s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: A central black creator dot is surrounded by colored agents. Text says creators can see what their content is worth to millions of agents and get paid accordingly, then calls the open web a miracle.
scenes.design: Small centered copy and a widening field of colored nodes.
scenes.purpose: State the creator benefit and return to the open-web theme.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 77–90s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: Index by Parallel remains centered on the light background.
scenes.purpose: Leave the product name as the final anchor.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 90–95.913s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

sound.detail: The draft coherently supports the open-web history, agent search, weakened advertising model and creator-payment argument. Several words are malformed, including coat/code and onred, so those fragments are not retained as literal wording. No validated listening or delivery/music/SFX assessment.
sound.visual_relation: V01–V08; script role only, sync unknown.

categories.finding: Small web → open possibilities → agent disruption → shrinking economics → new model → creator value/payment.
A tiny point and origin story invite attention through scale, but defer the product benefit.
Creators/content owners and agents become the clear participants late in the film, around 77–83s.
Node counts, grids, paths, circular masks and typography change across sampled states; exact easing and transition timing remain unchecked.
The repeated dot stands for a participant across the history, problem and proposed network, preserving visual continuity.
Dark fields shift to feed-hole paper and orange accents; colored nodes represent network variety.
Copy is often very small relative to the frame. Full-resolution frames clarify the late creator-value sentence, which is partly typed at 77s and complete at 79s.
The ASR draft supports the broad economic argument but contains malformed words. It provides script evidence only.
Music character and structure are unverified.
Effects and their sources are unverified.
categories.reason: No validated listening; waveform peaks do not identify effects.

categories.finding: Sound sync is unverified.
categories.reason: No validated listening or paired audiovisual timing.

categories.finding: The film uses abstract diagrams, paper texture and typography; actual production software is unknown.
Source duration 95.913 s; Watch metadata 1280 × 720. Frame rate, audio clipping and export quality not checked here.
categories.reason: Parent source metadata supports duration and dimensions; visual review is sampled.

categories.finding: Visible text and diagrams communicate a new creator-payment model, but no silent step-by-step workflow is shown.
A small central dot and sparse copy direct focus, while large dot fields show scale. Small text limits easy reading.
About two thirds of the film builds the historical/economic case before Index is introduced. The practical benefit arrives in the final fifth.
The opening network grows into a network of creators and agents, completing the metaphor rather than demonstrating a transaction.
The closing/opening fields may suggest loss and renewed possibility; viewer response is unmeasured.
The visual language is consistent, but the story stops before a content owner takes an action and receives a result.
The economics, valuation and payment statements are film claims. Participation terms, measurement and payments were not independently checked.
Orange emphasis, feed-hole paper and a recurring dot network give the brand a recognizable visual system.
Add one content-owner example after the new model is introduced.
categories.experiment: Show joining, one content-use event, its stated value and a payment result with clear labels.

categories.finding: For Tin, reuse one simple visual token across the problem and solution, then connect it to a real campaign artifact.
categories.experiment: Carry a brief card through generation, review and published output; show the actual result before the end card.

categories.finding: No human new-viewer test was performed.
categories.reason: The product summary is this model’s film-only reading.

categories.finding: Mobile preview and accessibility checks were not performed.
categories.reason: Contact sheets are evidence views, not a stated mobile preview or compliance test.

lessons.keep: Use one recurring visual token to connect the problem and proposed solution.
try: Show one content-owner use and payment example after introducing the model.
For Tin, carry a brief card through generation, review and the real output.
lessons.avoid: Making the economic argument so long that the actual user benefit arrives only near the end.
lessons.open: Joining, valuation method, payment terms, actual scale, exact motion and audio remain unresolved.

comparison.story: Web history → agent disruption → new economics → creator value/payment.
comparison.motion: Dot networks, circular fields and repeated typography; exact timing unchecked.
comparison.sound: Coherent broad ASR argument with malformed fragments; no validated listening.
comparison.texture: Dark fields, feed-hole paper and orange emphasis.
comparison.lesson: A consistent abstract system can explain a market change but still needs one concrete user transaction.

scope: sampled visual and story review; ASR and measured signal support; no validated audio listening
